headline: Constraint-based genome-scale models paired with learning surrogates and optimisation
label: Constraint Based Metabolic Network Models
summary: Learning-based surrogates and Bayesian optimisation are being paired with genome-scale constraint-based models across production and hepatic applications.
synthesis: The dominant thread is constraint-based genome-scale metabolic modelling applied to distinct questions. An integrative Yeast9 flux balance framework is combined with machine learning and Bayesian optimisation to predict and raise S. cerevisiae single-cell protein biomass flux. A multi-scale framework couples genome-scale constraint-based models with dynamic bioreactor simulation and uses a neural network surrogate. A reproducible dual-model study applies Recon3D and Human-GEM with FVA, pFBA and sensitivity analysis to hepatic ATP maintenance under stachyose-derived short-chain fatty acid scenarios. What is new is the pairing of constraint-based simulation with learning-based surrogates and optimisation, alongside explicit cross-model comparison. All three items are preprints, so the evidence remains preliminary.
